title: Week 18 Check-In · The Whipping Boy
description: This week you started The Whipping Boy and met two very different boys: a spoiled prince and Jemmy, the orphan boy who takes his punishments. You practiced conjunctions (and, but, so), the prefixes inter- and sub-, and vowel team syllables. Show what you know!

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses a conjunction to join two ideas?
options: The prince was spoiled, but Jemmy was clever.
The prince was spoiled but, Jemmy was clever.
The prince was spoiled. But Jemmy was clever.

questions.text: Combine these two sentences into one using a conjunction: “The prince could not write his name. Jemmy could read and write.”
Write your own compound sentence using “but” to show a difference between two characters or ideas.
questions.status: kept (one word: contrast → difference, the word the lessons use)

questions.text: The prefix inter- means “between.” Break apart the word interrupt. What does it mean?
questions.status: new (old Q4 tested over-, not taught)

questions.text: The prefix sub- means “under.” A subway train most likely runs —
questions.from: 18.1 Morphology (“What does a subway go under?”)

questions.text: Choose one: interrupt, interact, or international. Write a sentence that shows what the word means.
Each word has a vowel team. Write each word and split it into syllables with a slash mark (example: rain/bow). season · explain · railroad
questions.status: new (old Q7 tested closed syllables, not taught)

questions.text: A vowel team is two vowels that work together to make one sound. Explain this rule in your own words and give one example word.
Which word is split into syllables the wrong way?
questions.from: 18.3 Spelling (a team never gets split up)

questions.text: How are Jemmy and Prince Brat different, according to this passage? Use a detail from the text.
Jemmy sat in on the prince’s lessons, but only Jemmy learned. Why do you think Jemmy learned when the prince didn’t? What does this tell you about him?
Does it seem fair that Jemmy has to take the prince’s punishments? Use details from the passage to explain your thinking.

Model sentence: “The prince had everything — fine food, warm clothes, and a throne to sit on — but Jemmy had only his wits.” Notice how the dashes and the word “but” show a sharp difference. Write your own sentence that shows a difference between two characters, using this pattern.
Write 1–2 sentences describing what each boy wants at the start of the story. What does Prince Brat seem to want? What does Jemmy seem to want?

passage.title: Reading passage (summary of Ch. 1–2)
passage.text: The prince was known throughout the kingdom as Prince Brat. He had never been whipped in his life, for it was the law: no one was allowed to strike a prince. Jemmy had been brought to the castle to take his punishments for him. Jemmy had to sit close at hand during the prince’s daily lessons. The prince learned nothing — but Jemmy learned to read, write, and do sums.
